title: Lightning Strike 15 - SAR 21 Range
description: When you’re friends with someone, there may come a time when you share your toys. Singapore’s Infantry Regiment has the same idea at Exercise Lightning Strike.
keywords: Files from external sources with reviewed licenses, PD US Air Force, Video display resolution 1280 x 720, Videos of SAR-21

transcript.text: For a cavalry scout raised in Georgia, this is living the dream.
Run around, yell at each other and just be with great group of guys firing weapons all day long.
That's pretty much every little boy's dream, I think, growing up.
At Exercise Lightning Strike, Sergeant Matthew Stripplin and his fellow second brigade cavalry soldiers carry out that dream in Singapore.
Only with a weapon none of them had shot before.
The Singapore Assault Rifle 21st Century, or SART 21.
With the SART 21, we actually got an opportunity to come down here
and we could actually go through remedial actions and immediate actions, learn the weapon system.
Lightning Strike allows the soldiers to learn how the others operate.
On time, on target, carry out.
And learning the SART 21 was an introduction that made sense.
A lot of us have never seen one before, so just taking all that information
that they have and being able to blend it back and forth, hopefully we can come to a level where we can help each other out.
Stripplin's boyhood dream may seem simple to him, but here in Singapore, it supports the mission
of enhancing military relations with an ally.
Being able to actually accomplish that in a foreign country and actually learn all these individuals' names and who they are
and actually spend time with them and build bonds, so that just makes everything a lot better.
Staff Sergeant Mike Larmen, Exercise Lightning Strike, Singapore.
